title: Where can you fly direct from London City Airport?
author: Brogan
intro: London City has around 30 direct routes, nearly all in Europe and most with British Airways. Here's what flies, which routes are summer or ski-season only, and how to pick one.
seo_title: London City Airport: 30 direct routes, mostly BA (2026)
seo_description: Around 30 direct routes, nearly all European and most with BA: cities all year, Greek and Med islands in summer, ski flights in winter. Checked Oct 2026.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Direct routes:** around 30
- **Main airline:** British Airways
- **Longest flights:** about 3½ hours
- **Long-haul:** none

London City is a small airport in the Docklands with a short runway, so only smaller jets can use it. That means no long-haul flights, but lots of quick European city routes, a summer list of islands and beach towns, and ski flights in winter. We checked these routes in October 2026. Routes change every season, so check the airline's timetable before you plan a trip.

sections.heading: Who flies from London City
sections.text:
**British Airways** flies most routes, through its CityFlyer arm. A May 2026 count put its summer network at 24 destinations, not including the winter-only ski routes.

The other airlines mostly fly to their home hubs. Airport guides list:

- **Swiss** to Zurich.
- **KLM** to Amsterdam.
- **Aer Lingus** to Dublin.
- **Luxair** to Luxembourg.
- **LOT, Aurigny and ITA Airways**, on smaller routes.

These change more often than BA's routes, so check the airline's own site.

London City's big selling point is time. It's close to the City and Canary Wharf, the DLR stops at the terminal, and the walk from the door to the gate is short. Our guide to [how early to arrive at London City](/blog/how-early-should-you-arrive-at-london-city-airport) explains the timing.

sections.heading: City breaks all year
sections.text:
BA's year-round routes are mostly business cities, which also make good weekend breaks:

| City | Flights a week (summer 2026) | Good for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Amsterdam](/destinations/amsterdam) | 25+ | Canals, museums, a first city break |
| [Florence](/destinations/florence) | 14+ | Renaissance art and Tuscan food |
| [Milan](/destinations/milan) (Linate) | 14+ | Shopping, the Duomo, [Lake Como](/destinations/lake-como) |
| Rotterdam | 14+ | Modern architecture, the harbour |
| [Nice](/destinations/nice) | 9+ | The Riviera and the old town |
| [Dublin](/destinations/dublin) | 21+ | Pubs, music and a short hop |

BA also added **Madrid** in December 2025, a good pick for a winter break with more daylight. See our [Madrid guide](/destinations/madrid).

Tip: Milan flights go to Linate, which is much closer to the city centre than Malpensa, so you can be in the centre in under half an hour by metro.

sections.heading: Summer sun and islands
sections.text:
In summer, BA adds a list of beach and island routes, many only a few times a week:

- [Ibiza](/destinations/ibiza) and [Mallorca](/destinations/mallorca), for the Balearics.
- [Málaga](/destinations/malaga) for the Costa del Sol, and Faro for the [Algarve](/destinations/algarve), from May to October.
- **Olbia** for Sardinia's [Costa Smeralda](/destinations/costa-smeralda).
- [Skiathos](/destinations/skiathos) and [Thessaloniki](/destinations/thessaloniki) in Greece, and [Split](/destinations/split) in Croatia, from mid-June.
- **Bergerac** for the [Dordogne](/destinations/dordogne), in June to August.
- **Toulon**, new for summer 2026, twice a week from late May to the start of September, for [Saint-Tropez](/destinations/saint-tropez) and the Var.

Watch out: on twice-weekly routes, the timetable decides your trip length. Look at the flight days before you set your heart on a three-night break.

sections.heading: Ski flights in winter
sections.text:
In recent winters, BA has flown ski routes from London City to **Geneva**, **Chambéry** and **Innsbruck**, in the ski season from December to early spring. They suit a week in [Chamonix](/destinations/chamonix), [Val Thorens](/destinations/val-thorens) or around [Innsbruck](/destinations/innsbruck), or a winter weekend by [Lake Annecy](/destinations/annecy).

The ski timetable is published separately each year, so check BA's site for the 2026/27 season. Skis count as sports equipment, so add them to your booking rather than turning up with them.

Zurich is also handy for the Swiss Alps all year, and Swiss trains from the airport station to resorts like [Zermatt](/destinations/zermatt) and [Interlaken](/destinations/interlaken).

sections.heading: What London City doesn't have
sections.text:
- **No long-haul:** there are no direct flights to the USA, the Caribbean or Asia.
- **No Canaries:** the sun routes stop at Spain, Portugal and the Mediterranean.
- **No budget airlines:** fares are often higher than from Stansted, Luton or Gatwick, especially at peak times.

For longer trips, many people fly from London City to Amsterdam, Zurich or Dublin and change there. If it's all on one ticket, the airline looks after you if the first flight is late. Dublin also has US pre-clearance, so you go through American immigration before you fly.

sections.heading: How to pick a route
sections.text:
- **Start with the season:** city routes run all year, sun routes are mostly June to September, and ski flights run in winter.
- **Compare the whole journey,** not just the fare. From east or central London, London City can save an hour or more each way, which matters on a two- or three-night break.
- **Look at the flight days:** many of the leisure routes fly a few times a week, so be flexible with dates.

sections.heading: Where could you go from London City?
sections.text:
For a quick break, try [Florence](/destinations/florence), [Amsterdam](/destinations/amsterdam) or [Nice](/destinations/nice). For a summer week, look at [Mallorca](/destinations/mallorca), [Skiathos](/destinations/skiathos) or the [Dordogne](/destinations/dordogne). Browse the [city breaks](/destinations/city-breaks) and [ski holidays](/destinations/ski-holidays) pages for more ideas.

If everyone wants somewhere different, read our guide to [deciding where to go on holiday](/how-to-decide-where-to-go-on-holiday), or add a few ideas to somewhere.party and let the draw decide.

faqs.question: Which airlines fly from London City Airport?
faqs.answer: Mostly British Airways, through BA CityFlyer. Swiss, KLM, Aer Lingus, Luxair and a few others fly to their home hubs. Check the airline's site, as these routes change.

faqs.question: Can you fly long-haul from London City Airport?
faqs.answer: No. The runway is short, so only smaller aircraft can use it. For long-haul trips, people usually connect in Amsterdam, Zurich or Dublin, or fly from Heathrow.

faqs.question: Does London City Airport have flights to the Canaries?
faqs.answer: No, not as of October 2026. The closest sun routes are summer flights to Spain, Portugal, the Balearics and Greece.

faqs.question: Does easyJet or Ryanair fly from London City?
faqs.answer: No. London City has no budget airlines, so fares are often higher than from Stansted, Luton or Gatwick.
